import re

def detect(cell):
    # Clean cells should only contain patterns of ISSN (8 digits, sometimes with X at the end) and may also include versions with hyphen.
    # Dirty cells can include additional text, URLs, multiple ISSN separated by spaces or text, and non-standard patterns.
    clean_patterns = [
        r'^[0-9Xx]{8}$',  # Straight 8 digit pattern with or without leading zeros.
        r'^[0-9]{4}-[0-9Xx]{4}$',  # 4 digits - 4 digits pattern.
    ]
    
    dirty_patterns = [
        r'\b[DPdp]rint',  # Example of any additional text mixed with ISSN
        r'\bDO[- ]?[- \d\D]*',  # Variations of DO and related text
        r'\d{4}-\d{1,2}',       # Patterns like '1932-6203' with descriptive text.
        r'\bJan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec-\d{2}\b',  # Patterns referring to months and years
        r'[- ]*\d[Xx][- \dA-Za-z]+',  # Checks for the presence of an 'X' followed by text or numbers.
        r'(?:[0-9]{4}-){0,1}[0-9Xx]{3,9}[\s\S]*\b[0-9A-Za-zXx]+\b',  # Continuation of one ISSN followed by another (dirty)
    ]
    
    # Check if the cell matches any clean patterns.
    for pattern in clean_patterns:
        if re.fullmatch(pattern, cell):
            return False
    
    # Check if the cell matches any dirty patterns.
    for pattern in dirty_patterns:
        if re.search(pattern, cell):
            return True
    
    # If cell didn't match clean patterns and does not contain dirty patterns, return False (clean).
    return False

import re

def detect(cell):
    # Based on the samples, the clean cells can be described as:
    # - One or more digits ('[0-9]+') or
    # - Starting with a digit, followed by a comma and ending with a digit ('[0-9]+,[0-9]+')
    # Here we define a pattern for clean cells then use the negative lookahead to detect dirty cells.
    clean_pattern = re.compile(r'^[0-9]+$|^([0-9]+,[0-9]+)$')
    if not clean_pattern.search(cell):
        return True  # The cell is dirty if it does not match the clean pattern
    return False

import re

def detect(cell):
    if cell == '':
        return False
    # Define patterns for clean cells
    # Clean cells can be single digits, numbers, or ranges of numbers
    clean_pattern = re.compile(r'^\d+-\d+$|^(\d+|-)+\d*$')
    # Define patterns for dirty cells
    # Dirty cells typically contain irregular formats such as numbers with letters or special characters
    pattern_dirty = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z]+-[0-9]+|[0-9]+-[A-Za-z]+|[A-Za-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9]+|[A-Za-z-]+|^[0-9]+-[A-Za-z-]+$')
    is_clean = bool(clean_pattern.match(cell))
    is_dirty = bool(pattern_dirty.match(cell))
    return not is_clean and is_dirty
